text:
sam_support: Heads up — we're getting a customer escalation (fastchat) about a burst of 503s starting ~10:34 UTC. I can see a spike in upstream errors for hosted inference. Attaching the first runner logs we grabbed.

devbot: deploy: service/infer-runner v2.1.7 -> v2.1.8 started by @eng_deploy (note: rolling).

jamie_oncall: Oncall here, thanks. Are the 503s correlated to a specific model or region?

sam_support: fastchat is hitting hosted-us-west1, model: redwood/ggml-13b-q4_0 (they call with long_context). QPS looks normal but a subset of requests with ~12k token prompts cause failures.

maya_reliability: quick triage — worker PID 4321 exited SIGABRT right after a large CUDA allocation failed. Repro snippet from logs:

```
[infer-runner] 2026-03-17T10:34:12.321Z ERROR upstream: allocation failed: cudaMalloc failed (out of memory) 
[infer-runner] 2026-03-17T10:34:12.322Z FATAL signal 6 (SIGABRT) at 0x7ffddcc4: abort() called
#0  0x7f8a1c2b in __GI_abort() 
#1  0x7f8a2a1d in __gnu_cxx::__verbose_terminate_handler() 
#2  0x7f8a2a2f in __cxxabiv1::__terminate() 
#3  0x7f8a2a41 in std::terminate()
#4  0x55aa3b in runtime::handle_cuda_error()
```

maya_reliability: Notably, this isn't the usual PTX or illegal-instruction trace; memory pressure spikes then abort path triggers assert in our allocator wrapper. Looks tied to very large context + kv cache allocation for the q4 quant model.

alice_ml: The quantized runtime doesn't gracefully refuse huge seq lengths if kv prefetch is on. We had a change in v2.1.8 that touched prefetch behavior. Could be related to the rolling deploy.

eng_lead: If it's a deploy causality, we may have a bad kernel/allocator interaction under load. Can we confirm which version is running on the crashed nodes?

maya_reliability: Crash host log shows runner v2.1.8. Several crashed pods are on the same GPU type (A10G-like), memory free dip right before crash.

sam_support: Customer reports their requests used max_tokens=8192 and context concat from previous conversation (so effective seq ~ 12k). They said it worked previously but started failing at 10:34.

jamie_oncall: Immediate mitigation options: 1) route traffic for that customer to fallback CPU fleet (slower but stable), 2) pin customer to v2.1.7 if available, 3) temporarily deny requests with effective_seq > 9k at the gateway to avoid OOM. Which is fastest?

maya_reliability: CPU fallback + gateway reject is fastest. We can push a routing rule for tenant fastchat to CPU pool in ~4min (ops-runbook has the script). Also push a temporary rate limit / max_seq gate at the API layer.

ops_runbook_bot: runbook: apply-tenant-routing --tenant fastchat --target cpu-fallback-pool  # queued

devbot: rollout status: service/infer-runner v2.1.8 40% -> 2 nodes show repeated restarts.

alice_ml: Workaround in runtime: short-term patch to check effective_seq BEFORE allocating KV and return 413/429 style error or fallback. But that requires a hotfix build.

sam_support: I'll reply to customer: "We're investigating, temporarily routing your traffic to a stable CPU fallback and adding safeguards. We'll update within 30 min."

eng_lead: Action items:
- maya_reliability: collect core dumps + full alloc traces from crashed nodes (priority).
- alice_ml: reproduce locally with same model + prompt length; try to trigger allocator path.
- jamie_oncall: implement tenant routing + gateway max_seq rule.
- sam_support: keep customer updated and collect a sample request payload for repro (strip PII).

maya_reliability: Logged: upstream-3105556789-crash-dumps in S3, saved /var/crash/core. I'll attach the crash id.

jamie_oncall: Routing applied for fastchat -> cpu-fallback-pool. API gateway rule added: reject if effective_seq > 9000 (return 413).

sam_support: customer ping: "Thanks, 503s stopped immediately after your update, latency is higher but it's working. Please let us know when fixed." :relieved:

alice_ml: I reproduced OOM locally with a synthetic prompt sequence ~11.5k tokens and v2.1.8 flags: kv_prefetch=on, batch_size=16. Disabling kv_prefetch prevents the large contiguous alloc and the model survives (slower but stable).

eng_lead: Root cause hypothesis: change in v2.1.8 + quant/runtime interaction causes aggressive KV prefetch leading to a single huge cudaMalloc for KV that OOMs and triggers abort path.

maya_reliability: Next steps: 1) rollback v2.1.8 on hosted runners OR pin incoming traffic away from nodes running it, 2) prepare hotfix to add early effective_seq check and graceful fallback when KV allocation fails, 3) mk a postmortem with customer timeline.

sam_support: Customer happy for now. I'll schedule a follow-up call once we have a timeline.

devbot: deploy: rollback service/infer-runner to v2.1.7 initiated by @eng_deploy.

jamie_oncall: I'll keep this open — will update when rollback finishes and we confirm no further restarts.

eng_lead: Thanks team. Include the specific sample request from the customer (sanitized) in the incident ticket so ML can reproduce more precisely.

sam_support: Adding to incident ticket INC-2026-0031. Closing chat for now, will update in the ticket. :white_check_mark:
